ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=13$, and $BC=24$. Point $D$ is on $BC$ ($BD > CD$). $\triangle AED$ and $\triangle ACD$ are symmetric about line $AD$, with point $C$ being symmetric to point $E$. $AE$ intersects $BC$ at point $F$. $BE$ and $CE$ are connected. When $DE \perp BC$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ADE$? What is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct $AH \perp BC$ at $H$, \\
since $AB=AC=13$, $BC=24$, \\
thus $BH=CH=12$, \\
thus $AH= \sqrt{AB^{2}-BH^{2}} =5$, \\
since $\triangle AED$ and $\triangle ACD$ are symmetrical about the line $AD$, \\
thus $\angle ADC=\angle ADE$, $CD=DE$, \\
since $DE\perp BC$, \\
thus $\angle BDE=90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle ADE=90^\circ+\angle ADB=\angle ADC$, \\
thus $90^\circ+\angle ADB=180^\circ-\angle ADB$, \\
thus $\angle ADB=45^\circ$, \\
since $\angle AHC=90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle ADB=\angle HAD=45^\circ$, \\
thus $AH=HD=5$, $\angle ADE=\angle ADB+\angle BDE=\boxed{135^\circ}$, \\
thus $BD=12+5=17$, \\
thus $CD=DE=24-17=7$, \\
thus $CE= \sqrt{CD^{2}+DE^{2}} =7\sqrt{2}$, \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{135^\circ}$, $\boxed{7\sqrt{2}}$.

raw_record.original_question: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=24$. Point $D$ is on $BC$ with $BD>CD$. $\triangle AED$ and $\triangle ACD$ are symmetric about line $AD$, so point $C$ is symmetric to point $E$. $AE$ intersects $BC$ at point $F$. Segments $BE$ and $CE$ are drawn. When $DE \perp BC$, what is the measure of $\angle ADE$? What is the length of $CE$?
raw_record.answer: Construct $AH \perp BC$ at $H$. Since $AB=AC=13$ and $BC=24$, we have $BH=CH=12$, so $AH=\sqrt{AB^2-BH^2}=5$. Since $\triangle AED$ and $\triangle ACD$ are symmetric about line $AD$, we have $\angle ADC=\angle ADE$ and $CD=DE$. Since $DE\perp BC$, $\angle BDE=90^\circ$. Thus $\angle ADE=90^\circ+\angle ADB=\angle ADC$, so $90^\circ+\angle ADB=180^\circ-\angle ADB$, hence $\angle ADB=45^\circ$. Since $\angle AHC=90^\circ$, $\angle ADB=\angle HAD=45^\circ$, so $AH=HD=5$. Therefore, $\angle ADE=\angle ADB+\angle BDE=135^\circ$. Also, $BD=12+5=17$, so $CD=DE=24-17=7$, and $CE=\sqrt{CD^2+DE^2}=7\sqrt{2}$. Therefore, the answers are $135^\circ$ and $7\sqrt{2}$.

Reasoning: Draw AH perpendicular to BC at H. Because AB=AC=13 and BC=24, in isosceles triangle ABC, H is the midpoint of BC, BH=CH=12, AH=sqrt(13^2-12^2)=5. Let x=angle ADB. Since B, D, C are collinear, angle ADC=180°-x. Also DE is perpendicular to BC, so angle BDE=90°, and thus angle ADE=90°+x. The problem states that C and E are symmetric about AD, so angle ADE=angle ADC, hence 90°+x=180°-x, solving gives x=45°.
In right triangle AHD, D, H, B are collinear, so angle ADH=angle ADB=45°, therefore AHD is a 45-45-90 triangle, obtaining AH=HD=5. Thus BD=BH+HD=12+5=17, CD=BC-BD=24-17=7. By symmetry CD=DE, so DE=7. Also because CD is perpendicular to DE, triangle CDE is a right isosceles triangle, so CE=7sqrt(2). Therefore angle ADE=135°, CE=7sqrt(2).
